---
title: "Evaluation Of <I>Vamana</I> And <I>Virechana</I> As Interventions To Decelerate The Aging Process In Healthy Adult Volunteers: Protocol For An Exploratory Single-Arm Clinical Trial"
description: The paper outlines a clinical trial protocol to investigate if traditional Ayurvedic purification therapies can influence biological markers associated with the aging process in healthy adults, with preliminary findings suggesting an increase in antioxidant levels and a decrease in oxidative stress markers after one intervention.
author: Gemini
date: 2026-09-27

---
Many traditional health systems explore ways to promote well-being and potentially slow down the aging process. One such approach involves ancient purification techniques, often performed seasonally, which aim to cleanse the body.

Researchers are now investigating these traditional methods, specifically two procedures known as therapeutic emesis (a controlled vomiting process) and therapeutic purgation (a controlled cleansing of the bowels). The goal is to see if these interventions can influence key biological indicators related to aging.

The study focuses on measuring changes in certain substances in the blood. These include malondialdehyde, which is a sign of cell damage from stress, and total superoxide dismutase, an enzyme that acts as the body's natural defense against such damage. They also look at telomerase activity, an enzyme crucial for maintaining the protective caps on our chromosomes, which are linked to how our cells age.

By carefully observing these markers before and after the purification treatments, scientists hope to understand if these traditional practices can indeed contribute to a healthier aging process by reducing cellular stress and supporting cellular repair mechanisms.
